## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle update loop can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
Working set is 68·N, with L1d spill at N≈481, L2 at N≈7710, and L3 at N≈246723. At q=0.01, ns/p is flat at 7.706–7.703 from N=10000 to N=100000 — both L3-resident (680 KB and 6.8 MB, within the 16 MB L3). A clear knee appears at the L3→DRAM spill: N=1000000 jumps to 10.98 ns/p, holding at 10.569 for N=10000000. The L2 spill at N≈7710 falls just below the first measurement point and shows no penalty, absorbed by L3. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: at q=0.5 the L3-resident flat region sits at ~17.4 ns/p versus ~7.7 at q=0.01, and the DRAM region at ~19 versus ~11, preserving the same knee at N≈246723.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.83 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01 — 69.6% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth falls with churn: 7.19 GB/s (57%) at q=0.1, 5.52 GB/s (44%) at q=0.25, 3.91 GB/s (31%) at q=0.5. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: frontend_stall dominates at 63–75% of cycles across all regimes, backend_stall is ~0%, and compute is only 25–41%. Frontend pressure worsens past the L3 spill, rising from 63.4% at N=10000 to 74.6% at N=1000000 (q=0.01), which explains the bandwidth drop from 8.83 to 6.19 GB/s — a code-delivery wall, not a memory wall.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize across particles. The update loop processes one particle at a time using scalar SSE (`vmulss`, `vaddss`, `vucomiss`) with limited component-wise packed ops (`vmulps`, `vaddps` on 128-bit xmm) operating within a single particle's position/velocity. There is no gather; particle data is loaded sequentially via `vmovups` from r14 at stride 0x44 (68 bytes) and `vmovsd`. The render path uses `vpaddusb` for packed saturating byte-adds on 8-byte pixel chunks in its fast path, but most pixel writes are scalar byte-by-byte: repeated `movzx`/`add`/`cmovb`/`mov BYTE PTR` sequences per R, G, B channel. The 304-instruction body with 30+ branches (`jmp`=6, `jbe`=6, `je`=5, `jae`=5, `jne`=4) creates a large, scattered code footprint that directly drives the 63–75% frontend stalls. The histogram reports zero vector-suffixed (wide packed) instructions, confirming no ymm/zmm usage.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 69.6% of the streaming ceiling (8.83 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01) and is frontend-bound at every measured regime, with frontend_stall at 63–75% and backend_stall near 0%. The compiler auto-vectorized only within single particles (`vmulps` on xmm), not across particles, and the 304-instruction branchy step function caps achievable bandwidth through instruction-delivery stalls rather than memory limits. Death rate raises the floor from 8.83 to 3.91 GB/s (31% of ceiling at q=0.5) without changing the N-shape, confirming the branchy respawn scales linearly with churn but the fundamental bottleneck is frontend, not bandwidth.
